issues.legal_issue: A transferee from a person who has attained majority may sue to set aside an unauthorized alienation of that person’s property made by a natural guardian during minority when the transferred right is an interest in property rather than a bare right to sue.
material_facts: A natural guardian sold the minor’s immovable property without obtaining the required court permission and without legal necessity.
After attaining majority, the former minor transferred the property to the plaintiff within the applicable limitation period.
The plaintiff sued to set aside the guardian’s sale and recover possession of the property.
issues.conclusion: The transferee was competent to bring the suit. The former minor had transferred an assignable interest in the property, not merely a bare right to sue, so the bar on transferring a mere right to sue did not prevent the action.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 8(3) of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956, a disposal of immovable property by a natural guardian contrary to the statutory requirements is voidable at the instance of the minor or any person claiming under the minor; that expression includes a purchaser from the former minor. Section 6(e) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, which bars transfer of a mere right to sue, must be read harmoniously with section 8(3): the right to defeat an adverse claim arising from a voidable guardian’s sale is an assignable interest in property, not a bare right to litigate. Section 5(b) of the Guardianship Act supports avoiding an unduly restrictive construction of the Act’s protections. The Court followed The J.K. Cotton Spinning & Weaving Mills Co. Ltd. v. State of Uttar Pradesh, Ashoka Marketing Ltd. v. Punjab National Bank, Palaniappa Goundan v. Nallappa Goundan, and P. Kamaraju v. C. Gunnayya, and rejected the contrary approach in Jhaverbhai Hathibhai Patel v. Kabhai Bechar Patel, Mon Mohan Bhattacharjee v. Bidhu Bhusan Dutta, and Palani Goundan v. Vanjiakkal.

rule.if: suit_challenges_guardian_alienation and guardian_was_natural_guardian and (guardian_lacked_required_approval or alienation_lacked_minor_benefit) and former_minor_transferred_property_interest and suit_brought_within_limitation

predicates.suit_challenges_guardian_alienation: The claimant brought a suit seeking to undo a transfer of property made during the owner’s minority by a guardian.
predicates.guardian_was_natural_guardian: The person who made the transfer acted as the minor’s natural guardian.
predicates.guardian_lacked_required_approval: The natural guardian made the property transfer without obtaining the required court approval.
predicates.alienation_lacked_minor_benefit: The guardian’s transfer was not made for the minor’s benefit or legal necessity.
predicates.former_minor_transferred_property_intere: After attaining majority, the former minor transferred to the claimant an interest in the property affected by the guardian’s sale.
predicates.suit_brought_within_limitation: The claimant brought the suit within the applicable limitation period.

issues.definition: When a suit challenges a natural guardian’s unauthorized or non-beneficial transfer, the former minor transferred an interest in the affected property, and the suit is timely, the transferee may sue to set aside the guardian’s transfer.
